notes: Klipsch La Scala II exact-model sheet V03 (2017): 51 Hz–17 kHz ±4 dB; 105 dB at 2.83 V/1 m, with the sheet footnoting sensitivity as measured in an average listening room; 100 W / 400 W handling (only the continuous 100 W scalar is stored); 8 ohm nominal impedance; K-33-E 15-inch woofer and three-way design. frequencyResponse.pointsContext: Klipsch-published on-axis frequency-response table; measured at 1 m; table heading states dB with 0 = 100 dB SPL. These are the source's tabulated values, retained without curve fitting.

notes: The source is Klipsch's exact original FORTÉ brochure; it documents 98 dB SPL at 1 W/1 m, 8 ohms, 100 W maximum continuous handling, a three-way vented design, a front 12-inch woofer, and a rear 12-inch passive 'drone'. The official on-axis response table is imported as 28 raw tabulated points, not digitized or curve-fitted; its context is 1 m and 0 dB = 100 dB SPL. For response-only DSP use, the model normalizes those points at 1 kHz so the separate 98 dB sensitivity remains the loudness reference. The same brochure's 32 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB bandwidth statement conflicts with its tabulated low-frequency values (for example, 30 Hz = −8 dB and 40 Hz = −4 dB); both are preserved as published, and the measured points are not used to rewrite the bandwidth field. No off-axis directivity data were found in this source. Source: https://assets.klipsch.com/product-specsheets/forte-brochure.pdf.
